note: Curated PUBLIC-DOMAIN nursery-rhyme lyrics for pipeline.kidsong.lyrics (config kidsong.lyrics_source = 'public_domain').
ONLY THE WORDS come from the public domain. The MELODY is generated fresh by ACE-Step for every episode from the
'song_style' caption below — no existing recording, arrangement or tune is used, sampled or imitated. That is what
keeps these episodes clear of both copyright and YouTube Content ID: a public-domain text set to a newly generated
melody contains no protected element at all. Note that many familiar TUNES are also public domain but their modern
RECORDINGS and ARRANGEMENTS are not, which is exactly why we never reuse a tune.
Inclusion rule: every entry must be traceable to a specific pre-1929 publication (public domain in the US as an
expired term, and long past life+70 for the named authors). Anything that could not be dated confidently was left
'adaptation' on each entry records exactly where the text deviates from its source. Deviations are kept minimal and
exist only to fit the channel format (3-5 verses of 2-4 short lines, a repeated hook, <= 9 words per line) and the
content rules (toddler-safe, the channel's own fixed cast).

excluded.The Wheels on the Bus: Verna Hills, 1939 — too recent, still in copyright in the US.
excluded.If You're Happy and You Know It: 20th-century origin, disputed and undatable. Cannot be shown to be public domain.
excluded.Head, Shoulders, Knees and Toes: The lyric is 20th-century and undated (the tune is older). Excluded.
excluded.The Itsy Bitsy Spider: The standard children's text cannot be sourced to a pre-1929 printing; the 1910 'Spider Song' printing has different, unusable words.
excluded.A-Tisket, A-Tasket: The traditional text is old, but the familiar version is Ella Fitzgerald's 1938 copyrighted adaptation — too easy to drift into.
excluded.Old MacDonald Had a Farm: The 1917 'Tommy's Tunes' (F. T. Nettleingham) text IS public domain and would have been legal to use. Excluded on QUALITY grounds instead: its 'Ee-i-ee-i-oh' vocable refrain has no rhyme scheme and no stable syllable count, so it cannot pass the meter/rhyme gate in script_qc without weakening that gate for every other song.
excluded.Humpty Dumpty / Jack and Jill / Little M: Public domain, but excluded on content: a fall, a head injury, a frightening spider, and a falling cradle are not toddler-safe for this channel.

songs.title: Twinkle, Twinkle, Little Star - A Gentle Sing-Along for Toddlers
songs.description: A calm, cozy sing-along about the stars in the night sky. Clap and count along with us! #kidssong #nurseryrhyme #toddlersongs #singalong #bedtimesong
songs.song_style: children's nursery rhyme, gentle calm lullaby, cute female child voice, soft simple melody, twinkly bells, slow bouncy tempo, warm and cozy
songs.subject_description: a small glowing golden five-pointed star with a gentle smiling face
songs.canonical_setting: a cozy backyard at night with a deep blue starry sky and a soft picnic blanket on the grass

source.author: Jane Taylor
source.publication: Rhymes for the Nursery, by Ann and Jane Taylor (London, 1806)
source.public_domain: Published 1806; Jane Taylor died 1824. Expired copyright in the US (pre-1929) and worldwide (life+70 ended 1894).
source.adaptation: Verses 1, 2 and 4 of Taylor's poem, verbatim. Taylor's verse 3 ('When the blazing sun is gone...') is dropped for length. The two-line hook ('Clap and sing along with me / Twinkle, twinkle, one, two, three') is NEWLY WRITTEN for this channel, not Taylor's.

lines: Twinkle, twinkle, little star
How I wonder what you are
verses.scene_hint: The three toddlers sit on a soft blanket in a garden at dusk, looking up at a sky full of big friendly cartoon stars.

lines: Up above the world so high
Like a diamond in the sky
verses.scene_hint: The toddlers point up at one enormous glowing star, their faces lit warm by its light.

lines: Clap and sing along with me
Twinkle, twinkle, one, two, three
verses.scene_hint: The toddlers clap their hands together and count on their fingers under the starry sky, grinning at the camera.

lines: Then the traveller in the dark
Thanks you for your tiny spark
verses.scene_hint: A tiny star-shaped lantern glows on the grass beside the toddlers as they cup their hands around its light.

lines: Clap and sing along with me
Twinkle, twinkle, one, two, three
verses.scene_hint: The toddlers clap their hands together and count on their fingers under the starry sky, grinning at the camera.

songs.title: Zuri Had a Little Lamb - A Happy Sing-Along Song for Toddlers
songs.description: The little lamb follows along everywhere! Clap your hands and sing this classic with us. #kidssong #nurseryrhyme #toddlersongs #singalong #animalsong
songs.song_style: children's nursery rhyme, cheerful upbeat kids song, cute female child voice, simple very repetitive catchy melody, gentle bouncy tempo, playful, bright, warm
songs.subject_description: a small fluffy white lamb, knee-high to the children, with a soft white fleece and gentle dark eyes
songs.canonical_setting: a sunny country lane beside a small schoolhouse, with green fields and a soft dirt path

source.author: Sarah Josepha Hale
source.publication: Poems for Our Children (Boston: Marsh, Capen & Lyon, 1830)
source.public_domain: Published 1830; Hale died 1879. Expired copyright in the US (pre-1929) and worldwide (life+70 ended 1949).
source.adaptation: Hale's stanzas 1-3, with two changes: the name 'Mary' is replaced with 'Zuri' throughout so the song stars this channel's fixed cast rather than introducing an outside character, and stanza 1's 'And everywhere that Mary went' keeps Hale's wording with only that substitution. The two-line hook is NEWLY WRITTEN. Hale's stanzas 4-6 (the teacher's moral) are dropped for length.

lines: Zuri had a little lamb
Its fleece was white as snow
Everywhere that Zuri went
The lamb was sure to go
verses.scene_hint: Zuri walks along a sunny country path with a fluffy white cartoon lamb trotting close behind her.

lines: He followed her to school one day
Which was against the rule
It made the children laugh and play
To see a lamb at school
verses.scene_hint: The lamb peeks around the doorway of a bright little schoolroom while Kofi and Nala laugh and point.

lines: Little lamb, come sing with me
Clap your hands and count to three
verses.scene_hint: The three toddlers kneel in the grass around the lamb, clapping their hands and counting on their fingers.

lines: And so the teacher turned him out
But still he lingered near
He waited on the step outside
Till Zuri did appear
verses.scene_hint: The lamb waits patiently on the grass outside a low window, tail wagging, while sunshine falls across the yard.

lines: Little lamb, come sing with me
Clap your hands and count to three
verses.scene_hint: The three toddlers kneel in the grass around the lamb, clapping their hands and counting on their fingers.

source.author: Traditional (English)
source.publication: First recorded in Thomas D'Urfey's play The Campaigners (1698); printed as a nursery rhyme in Tommy Thumb's Pretty Song Book (c. 1744).
source.public_domain: Anonymous traditional text recorded from 1698; long out of copyright everywhere.
source.adaptation: Verse 1 is the traditional couplet verbatim.
